newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium slumps to fresh 2-1/4 year LME lows.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium slumps to fresh 2-1/4 year LME lows.

text.p: Aluminium prices spiralled lower during early Thursday London Metal Exchange (LME) trading, with the market notching up fresh 2-1/4 year lows.
Traders said the breach of the previous low at $1,357 a tonne sent prices down to $1,348, a $29 loss from Wednesday.
Aluminium slumps to fresh 2-1/4 year LME lows =2
They said the latest fall in aluminium prices was sparked by a slump in copper -- the LME market-leader -- which dropped under $1,900.

Once aluminium dropped under $1,357, sell-stops (automatic liquidation orders) kicked in and pushed prices down to the lows. Traders now see the market in danger of falling further and hitting $1,330 and then $1,300.

Supply/demand factors lie behind the decline, with Europe's Aluminium Association forecasting on Wednesday a drop in European demand. Inventory levels are rising, so aluminium consumers can bide their time when purchasing.
